newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SA will respond 'very positively' to U.N. -- Mandela.
newsitem.headline: SA will respond 'very positively' to U.N. -- Mandela.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela said on Tuesday that the United Nations could count on the South African government responding "very positively" to any request for help in stemming the refugee crisis in Zaire.

Mandela, reacting to an appeal by African leaders for the U.N. Security Council to send a neutral force quickly to eastern Zaire to help 1.2 million Hutu refugees facing famine and epidemic, told reporters: "Any request from the United Nations, we will respond to very positively in accordance with our capacity."
Mandela would not be drawn on the possible nature of any South African involvement, but reiterated that he respected the opinions of the continent's leaders.

"We will respond to any call made to us by the United Nations, by the Organisation of African Unity (OAU), and by the leaders in the region -- in whom we have the greatest confidence," he said in impromptu remarks after a dinner function.
The South African president said last week the government was willing to assist the U.N. in Zaire, but did not want to act without the backing of the region's leaders.
"It would be a mistake to expect South Africa to act unilaterally," he said.
